items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: I mentioned that Louie thing because that little introduction always knocked me out. ... Louie perhaps did it more than anybody but Joe Oliver

ctx.x: and it doesn't take, it takes a lot of work. But when you say off the beat, do you mean two and four or do you mean like bumping, holding back a little?

Yeah, that's what I mean, holding back. Phrasing, see. Phrasing off the beat. A whole phrase off the beat. In other words, you could start ahead, you end up behind. Play behind, play ahead. Like Louie, see, he, on this tune once in a while, his little instrument goes, he goes, they start out one, two, one, two, see, he holds back and holds and I mentioned that Louie thing because that little introduction always knocked me out. Yeah, well, Louie perhaps did it more than anybody but Joe Oliver, in some respects was…
